# Target list: Fashion, apparel and colour (服飾與配色)

**DRAFT v0.1, written 2026-10-12. Generated by `render_lists.py` from `target-list-fashion.csv`: edit the CSV, not this page.** Nothing here has been sent, and **no row is a verified contact**: no primary page was opened, so every row is labelled `recalled` or `search summary` in the CSV `basis` column and must be checked by a person before use. Showroom persona for tracking only: **色環 (sehuan)** (B2B income belongs to the studio). Lead offer: B1 lookbook stills (face-free options first) and sponsored posts. Rate card and terms: [rate-card.md](../rate-card.md). Playbook: [outreach-playbook.md](outreach-playbook.md). Drafts: [email-drafts.md](email-drafts.md).

**Every row says "verify existence and current contact route".** Before a row is used, one person spends about five minutes to: (1) confirm the entity exists and still trades under this name, (2) find its official business-inquiry route, (3) read the page for any note that says it does not accept unsolicited proposals (if it does, mark the row do-not-contact), (4) fill `verified_on`. No email address, phone number or web address is recorded anywhere in this folder, on purpose: none was verified and none may be guessed.

**Count: 50 rows (P1 7, P2 13, P3 30). Actionable rows (P1 to P3): 50.**
The target of 50 is reached with entities I am confident exist, but see the weak point below.

**Legend.**

* **Pri:** P1 = most plausible reply to a small studio, contact first (after the gates and the warm route); P2 = plausible, contact after the P1 wave is answered; P3 = low reply likelihood (large group, multinational or publisher), supplier or partner route only, contact last; HOLD = do not contact until the stated condition is met; SKIP = never contact (Ground rule 6 or the decline list).
* **conf** (existence confidence, my judgement): high = well-known entity I am confident exists and trades in Taiwan; medium-high = confident it exists, less sure of its current name or scope; medium = recalled or seen only in a thin search summary, check first.
* **Route:** STD = official website contact form or listed business-inquiry page (to look up). ADV = STD, and also look for an advertiser, brand-cooperation or media-kit page (to look up). PTN = STD, and also look for a partner, reseller or agency-programme page (to look up). The CSV carries the full wording.
* **Template:** T1 = first contact for a brand; T2 = first contact for an agency, platform or vendor (both in [email-drafts.md](email-drafts.md)).
* **also:** the same entity is also a row in another list (F fashion, A AI tools, H home). It still counts as one entity: **one open thread per entity and per corporate group** (playbook section 5).
* **Status:** left empty on purpose; the humans fill it. Allowed values are in the playbook (section 6).

## Warm-contact route (the operator's note) and how to use this list

The operator has about five warm fashion contacts (`strategy/portfolio.md` hypothesis H5; `HUMAN_TODO.md` 11). **The project does not record who they are, so none is named here and none is invented.** The warm route comes first, before any cold row:

| Slot | Brand or person (real name, operator fills) | How the operator knows them | Said yes to a free private sample? | Can introduce a brand or agency from this list? | Notes |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| W1 | [TO FILL WHEN REAL] | [TO FILL WHEN REAL] | [TO FILL WHEN REAL] | [TO FILL WHEN REAL] | |
| W2 | [TO FILL WHEN REAL] | [TO FILL WHEN REAL] | [TO FILL WHEN REAL] | [TO FILL WHEN REAL] | |
| W3 | [TO FILL WHEN REAL] | [TO FILL WHEN REAL] | [TO FILL WHEN REAL] | [TO FILL WHEN REAL] | |
| W4 | [TO FILL WHEN REAL] | [TO FILL WHEN REAL] | [TO FILL WHEN REAL] | [TO FILL WHEN REAL] | |
| W5 | [TO FILL WHEN REAL] | [TO FILL WHEN REAL] | [TO FILL WHEN REAL] | [TO FILL WHEN REAL] | |

1. **Warm contacts are approached by the operator in person or by phone first, not by email.** Before the gates in the playbook close, the only thing the operator may say is the private, verbal version in `content/sehuan/b2b-pitch.md` A3 (the studio is exploring disclosed virtual-presenter creative, nothing exists yet, a free scoped sample is being planned, no price). No character name, no handle, no image.
2. **What to ask a warm contact** (b2b-pitch A5): which one or two products; product-only photographs with a written usage licence; whether they accept content that says in the picture and the caption that it is an AI-generated illustration; who approves; and whether a private sample (posted nowhere) is the right first step. Also ask for **one introduction** to a brand or agency on this list.
3. **If a warm contact works at, or can introduce, a brand on this list,** write that in the row's `warm_route_note` (CSV) and move the row up to P1. A warm introduction replaces the cold template; use T4 (reply to interest) wording as a guide, not T1.
4. **The weak point of this list, stated plainly.** The entities most likely to answer a two-person studio are small independent labels, and I cannot name them with confidence: the rows above are mostly well-known names (many large, several multinational). Small labels are best found by the operator and wife browsing Instagram and Pinkoi, then adding rows to the CSV (priority P1, `basis` = "found by the studio on <date>") after the five-minute verification above. Do not mass-contact designers found on Pinkoi.
5. **Lead with face-free options.** A photoreal virtual-model try-on (虛擬試穿示意) is ON HOLD until the lawyer answers (rate card section 0 item 5; b2b-pitch A2 gate 3). The first sample offered to a fashion contact is a colour-story board or a flat-lay lookbook layout built from the brand's own product photos (b2b-pitch A4 options 1 and 2).
6. **Cosmetic and skin products are declined** even where a publisher or department store sells them (Ground rule 6; `personas/sehuan/bible.md` 9.2). The full category list is [decline-list.md](../decline-list.md) section 2 (C01 to C33): check each brief against it, not only the row's flags.
